Money Market Funds: a good alternative to near-instant-access savings?
The Vanguard "Short Term Sterling Money Market Fund" is [currently on track](https://www.hl.co.uk/funds/fund-discounts,-prices--and--factsheets/search-results/v/vanguard-sterling-short-term-money-mrkt-class-a-income/charts) to pay out the equivalent of 5.3% (p.a.) this month.  This seems to beat any equivalent cash ISA (the best offering is 5.08% from Zopa) and avoids having to open a new ISA.  Royal London seems to have an even better offering which has peaked over 6%, but I'm less sure about access to that.

I get 4.84% with Chip and 5% with Barclays but both are exposed to tax once I have more than about £10k in savings.  

There's obviously no guarantee of returns with a MMF, and there's some small risk of the fund going wrong, but overall the risk is very low as I understand it. They're not quite instant access, as Vanguard usually take a few days to transfer out, but pretty close to, so probably good to have a reasonable emergency fund in an alternative product.

In particular it seems that these avoid the need to gamble on an ISA provider keeping rates competitive, since you can only open one cash ISA product per tax year.

Am I missing something here?  I don't see many people talking about these right now.
